MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  OCTOBER 10, 2016

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 6:00 p.m. to conduct interviews for the vacancies on the Park and Activities
and Planning Commissions.

  ***

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:13 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

Others Present:  Pam Schachter, Park and Activities Commission

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 27, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL requested the following correction under Item No.
  8B – PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 05-16 (THE VILLAGE/MERRILL GARDENS):

  “COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL……Finally she noted that the staff report
  does provide the findings to make a mitigated negative declaration on the
  environmental impact report.”

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL requested the following correction under Item No.
  10B – LANDSCAPE CONSULTANT SERVICES:

  “COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that SCAG is providing sustainable
  grants that may include applications for median landscaping projects.”

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 27, 2016
  AS AMENDED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
OCTOBER 10, 2016
 B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – SEPTEMBER AND OCTOBER

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 57449 THROUGH 57479 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $258,550.73; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 090116 THROUGH 090216;
  57311 THROUGH 57325; 57326; 57363 THROUGH 57387; 57388
  THROUGH 57390; 97391 THROUGH 97392; 57393 THROUGH 57399;
  57435 THROUGH 57441 IN THE AMOUNT OF $630,245.71 FOR A
  GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $888,796.44 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A AND B.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to
  the City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be
  read by title only.

B.  HABITAT CONSERVATION FUND PROGRAM APPLICATION RESOLUTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2387 approving
  an application for grant funds from the State of California's Habitat
  Conservation Program Wildlife Area Activities Grant to expand the hours of
  operations and programs offered at the George F Canyon Nature Center and
  Preserve.

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2387 APPROVING AN APPLICATION FOR
  GRANT FUNDS FROM THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA'S HABITAT
  CONSERVATION PROGRAM WILDLIFE AREA ACTIVITIES GRANT TO
  EXPAND THE HOURS OF OPERATIONS AND PROGRAMS OFFERED AT
  THE GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER AND PRESERVE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2387 by title only.

COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL pulled Item 6C. for discussion:

C.  ROADWAY SAFETY MASTER PLAN DEVELOPMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file this report.

  City Manager Prichard noted that this was brought to the City’s attention by
  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL regarding bicyclists and motorists working
  together to create a safe environment to travel throughout the Peninsula.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL also discussed this issue with Council Members
  from other cities noting that there may be some appropriate involvement at the
  elected officials’ level.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN commented that this could be a difficult task to
  undertake due to both bicyclists and motorists asserting incompatible
  positions.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 10, 2016
   MAYOR ZUCKERMAN and MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN volunteered to serve
  on an ad hoc committee with Palos Verdes Estates and Rancho Palos Verdes
  representatives as needed.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN

  TO APPOINT MAYOR ZUCKERMAN AND MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN
  TO SERVE ON AN AD HOC COMMITTEE WITH REPRESENTATIVES
  FROM THE CITIES OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES AND RANCHO PALOS
  VERDES TO DISCUSS BICYCLE SAFETY ON THE PENINSULA.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

  NONE

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

A.  CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING - PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 12-16
  (ORDINANCE NO. 707) (AMENDMENT TO SECTION 10.24.200 (PEDDLERS
  AND VENDORS) OF THE RHEMC); APPLICANT: CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES; LOCATION: CITY-WIDE

  Recommendation:  That the City Council:  1)  Continue to take public
  testimony; 2) Close the public hearing; 3) Discuss the issues; and 4) Conduct
  the second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 707.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN requested additional public testimony.

  No public testimony was offered.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 707
  AMENDING AND RESTATING SECTION 10.24.200 OF THE ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO MOBILE PEDDLER
  VEHICLE AND OPERATIONAL REGULATIONS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 707 by title only.

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF OCTOBER 3, 2016

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 3, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  COMMISSIONER EMAIL ADDRESSES

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize email accounts to be set up
  for Commission Members in the annual amount of $1,334.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  Discussion ensued regarding the cost of setting up each Commissioners’ email
  address.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 10, 2016
   Further discussion ensued with City Attorney Davis explaining the value of all
  City business being conducted via City devices and email accounts.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO AUTHORIZE EMAIL ACCOUNTS TO BE SET UP FOR COMMISSION
  MEMBERS IN THE ANNUAL AMOUNT OF $1,334.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  ORDINANCE NO. 709 - ADDING CHAPTER 17.47 TO THE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO SHORT-TERM RESIDENTIAL
  RENTALS

  Planning Director Wahba provided a brief staff report.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Planning Director Wahba noted that the
  enforcement plan will include notification of the major internet sites that this
  ordinance is in place along with intermittent investigation of postings on
  various websites.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 709.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 709 by title only.

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

A.  City Attorney Davis suggested discussing the implications of the marijuana
  initiative that is on the November ballot, if it should pass, at a future meeting.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 26, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF
  SEPTEMBER 26, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that a proposed dressage arena was discussed
  on the Palos Verdes Landfill. She indicated that City Manager Prichard,
  Community Services Director Clark and she will look at ways to better engage
  with the community on potential projects such as this one.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that she received good feedback regarding the
  City Celebration and reiterated her appreciation to Park and Activities
  Commissioner Pam Schachter for the successful equestrian events.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 10, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL also thanked Park and Activities Commissioner
  Schachter and the community for an enjoyable event and believed that everyone
  was pleased with the new location.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN was also pleased to announce that the City won the
  volleyball game against the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department.

B.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE COMMITTEE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 29,
  2016

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE COMMITTEE
  MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 29, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF noted that the date for the Holiday Parade is Saturday,
  December 3. She then announced The Promenade Tree Lighting scheduled for
  Saturday, November 19 at 5:00 p.m.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted her concern with allowing a horse-drawn
  carriage to go through The Promenade because of the close proximity of the
  spectators to the horses.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN inquired if the City Celebration Subcommittee has
  considered altering the Holiday Parade route since Peninsula Center is a primary
  retail base.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that he received many comments complaining about
  the long intervals between participants. COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ responded
  that the route change for 2016 is designed to address this very problem.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  COMMISSIONER APPOINTMENTS

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that he was very impressed with all the applicants
  and thanked those who interviewed for the various positions.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPOINT BRIDGET CARMAN TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION AND
  MICHAEL GIGLIA AND KIRK RETZ TO THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  GENERAL PLAN COMMITTEE UPDATE

  Planning Director Wahba provided a brief update.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that he attended the first meeting via phone
  conference.

  After brief discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL

  TO HAVE AN UPDATE PROVIDED BY STAFF FOR THE COUNCIL AFTER
  EACH SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 10, 2016
 C.  MEETING SCHEDULE AND MEETING PLACE FOR GROUP DYNAMICS
  WORKSHOP

  After brief discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to meet on the
  following dates:

  October 24 – Compensation Study Workshop
  October 25 – Regular City Council Meeting
  November 1 – City Celebration Debriefing Meeting
  November 14 – Group Dynamics and Community Workshop
  (Location: Good Stuff Restaurant)
  November 15 – Adjourned City Council Meeting
  December 13 – Regular City Council Meeting

  ***

  At 8:25 p.m., the City Council convened into Closed Session.

  ***

14.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  DISCUSSION WITH RESPECT TO PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT:  CITY MANAGER
  QUARTERLY EVALUATION
  (Pursuant to Government Code Section 54937)

  ***

  At 10:08 p.m., the COUNCIL reconvened into open session with MAYOR
  ZUCKERMAN, MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, COUNCILWOMAN HUFF,
  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, and COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ present.

  ***

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO DIRECT THAT AN AMENDMENT TO THE CITY MANAGER’S
  CONTRACT BE PREPARED FOR COUNCIL APPROVAL TO REINSTATE
  THE PARS PROGRAM AT PREVIOUSLY FUNDED LEVEL FOR FY16-17.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

15.  ADJOURNMENT TO MONDAY, OCTOBER 24, 2016 AT 5:30 P.M. FOR THE
  PURPOSE OF CONDUCTING A COMPENSATION/SALARY ADMINISTRATION
  WORKSHOP

  At 10:08 p.m. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN formally adjourned the City Council
  meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
Deputy City Clerk  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
OCTOBER 10, 2016
